clue.text: One or two birds of prey

definitions.text: One or two birds of prey

parts.words: One or two birds of prey
parts.note: the name can be read as a single large hunting bird or as two separate raptors, a bird of the genus Aquila followed by a nocturnal hunter

explanation.walkthrough: Taken as one hyphenated word it is a single species, the largest of the owls; split at the hyphen it names two different birds of prey, hence 'one or two'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a huge Eurasian owl species, a raptor whose name happens to join two other raptor names.

clue.text: Make difference to morale as a close friend

parts.note: to alter something is to make a difference to it
ego is one's self-esteem or confidence, akin to morale

explanation.surface: A trusted companion can change your spirits for the better.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally 'other self', it means a trusted companion as close as a second self.

clue.text: Inflamed around middle — it's not serious

indicators.note: the lit word goes around the centre word

parts.note: something set alight has been lighted
the heart of something is its middle

explanation.surface: A doctor reassures a patient that the swelling in their midriff is nothing to worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflamed around middle' sounds medical, but 'inflamed' means set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheerful and carefree means not taking things gravely.

clue.text: Start a betting scheme that's easy to understand

parts.note: to open is to start
a bookmaker's book records the bets taken on an event

explanation.surface: A bookie launches a wager system that punters find simple to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something transparent and readily comprehended is said to be like a volume left lying unclosed for all to read.

clue.text: Person who wants to be heard in Japan, perhaps

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so the person-who-lacks word gives the sound of the letters entered

parts.note: one who lacks something, who wants for it, is a lacker

explanation.surface: A visitor to Tokyo is eager to get a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Japan here is not the country but a hard black varnish, originally from Japan; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a glossy black varnish, one kind of hard decorative coating.

clue.text: Run English history — make a meal of it

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
history is the past

explanation.surface: A tutor tells a student to tackle English history and make a feast of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a meal of it' is an idiom for overdoing a task; here 'make' and 'of it' are links and 'meal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for food taken at a sitting, a meal.

clue.text: Knowing it's outmoded as fashion

definitions.meaning: an archaic noun meaning manner or way, surviving in phrases like 'in no ...' and suffixes like clockwise

explanation.surface: A sharp observer remarks that the style is out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reads as clothing style but means manner or way, and 'outmoded' warns the sense is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means sagacious; the old noun means manner, way of doing something.

clue.text: Twice as keen, perhaps, as this venomous creature

indicators.note: suggests the letters might be arranged some other way, so they are shuffled
the little word 'as' is taken two times over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dangerous serpent is said to be doubly sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles AS to ASAS; with KEEN that gives eight letters, rearranged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are venomous reptiles of tropical oceans, serpents living in salt water.

clue.text: Unattractive combination of states I have formed

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly, so 'states' gives avers
taken as written
VE is the contracted form of have, as in I've

explanation.surface: A political scientist finds an alliance of nations formed by me rather off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination of states' suggests a federation, but 'states' is a verb here; 'combination' and 'formed' just tell you to join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that repels or causes avoidance is off-putting, the opposite of attractive.

clue.text: As a fast runner, he's out on his own

definitions.meaning: a male deer, an animal noted for its speed
going to a party without a partner, or a men-only night out, is going this way

explanation.surface: A sprinter is left alone, out in front of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A male red deer is swift on its feet, and a man attending alone or at an all-male party is said to go this way.

clue.text: Does have accommodation in the rear

indicators.note: the word hinds holds the lodgings word within it, as a house has guests in
the word hinds holds the lodgings word within it, as a house has guests in

parts.note: female deer are does, also called hinds
quarters are lodgings or accommodation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is room for lodging out at the back of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is the plural noun for female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The back part of an animal, especially a horse, is its rear end or haunches.

clue.text: Commons supporting policy of Charles I, in a way

indicators.note: in a down clue the food word sits beneath the policy word, holding it up

parts.note: 'Thorough' was the name of the strict policy of Strafford and Laud under Charles I
commons are rations or food provided, and fare is food

explanation.surface: The House of Commons backing a royal policy of Charles I, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' looks like the House of Commons, but means food rations; 'Thorough' was a 1630s policy of rigorous royal rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A public road or street is a way through a place.

clue.text: Parisian I almost cast as priest

parts.note: the French for I is je, as a Parisian would say

indicators.note: drop the final letter, so the throwing word stops one short of complete

parts.note: to cast is to throw

explanation.surface: A Frenchman nearly gets picked for the role of a cleric in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible this man is the priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses; 'cast' suggests theatre but means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus he is described as the priest of Midian, whose daughter married Moses.

clue.text: Those in a newly liberated country

indicators.note: the letters are made afresh into a new arrangement, as a country is newly formed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about the people living in a nation recently freed from occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the old spelling of Estonia, the Baltic state that regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic republic broke free of Soviet rule in 1991, so it was then a freshly independent nation.

clue.text: Indians from Missouri — those on the warpath?

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
hawks are aggressive people who favour war, the opposite of doves

explanation.surface: Native Americans come from a western state, war-painted and ready for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the warpath' fits the Native American picture but here means the war party of politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a tribe of Native Americans of the Iroquois confederacy, once commonly called Indians.

clue.text: Fashion badly needing change of emphasis

definitions.text: Fashion badly needing change of emphasis

indicators.note: the stress must move from the first word to the second, so the two are read in swapped order

parts.note: the prefix mis- means badly or wrongly
to fashion is to shape

explanation.surface: A designer's work is poor and needs a shift in focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing change of emphasis' tells you to swap the two words round, giving 'badly fashion', prefix first.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape something wrongly, to deform it, is to make it badly.

clue.text: Nothing amidships is in this style

indicators.note: the zero sits amid the ship, inside its letters

parts.note: a barque is a kind of sailing ship
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A design note: nothing is placed in the middle of the vessel in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidships' is a nautical word for the middle of a ship, but it splits into 'amid' (inside) and 'ships' (a barque).
explanation.definitionFit: It is an ornate artistic and architectural manner of the 17th and early 18th centuries.

clue.text: From birth, having chance of success in a short life

indicators.note: the in-the-running words go inside the short life story

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story
someone still in it has a chance of winning

explanation.surface: A newborn with a promising start but a brief life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase literally means 'from the beginning'; 'life' is a written life, a biography.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means from the very beginning, from the start.

clue.text: Understood it might be signalled?

definitions.meaning: understood means implied or tacit, taken for granted without being said
a message conveyed by signs or flags is not voiced, hence not said aloud

explanation.surface: A message was grasped, presumably passed on by signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An implicit agreement is tacit; something signalled rather than said was never voiced.

clue.text: Corrupt leader of plot put on phoney accent

indicators.note: in a down clue the initial letter is placed on top of what follows
the first letter heads the word plot
the accent is fake, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crooked ringleader puts on a fake accent to disguise himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' is an adjective meaning sinful; 'put on' is a charade instruction, not affecting an accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Peccant means sinning or guilty of wrongdoing, morally rotten.

clue.text: Becoming blue? It's a mistake

indicators.note: the letters are written in error, jumbled into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks if blue suits them, then decides it was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' means fitting or flattering, an adjective, not the verb it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: A becoming outfit is appropriate and flattering, fitting the wearer well.

clue.text: French language in British school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: French is taught at a British school.
explanation.walkthrough: It is the Celtic language of Brittany in north-western France; ETON is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celtic tongue of Brittany is spoken in France.

clue.text: Scoff playfully, say

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so 'in jest' gives the sound of the letters entered

parts.note: doing something playfully is doing it in jest

explanation.surface: Someone mocks, but only teasingly, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mocking, which fits 'playfully', but the sense is eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it up, to take it into the body.

clue.text: Long to embrace Desdemona, initially? Main cause of her tragedy

indicators.note: the longing word wraps its arms around the initial letter

parts.note: to long for something is to hanker after it

indicators.note: take the first letter of the name Desdemona

parts.note: main means principal or chief

explanation.surface: A question about Othello: did yearning to hold Desdemona chiefly bring about her doom?
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Othello, the strawberry-spotted one Desdemona drops and Iago plants on Cassio convinces Othello of her guilt, leading to her murder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello, the lost keepsake Iago uses as false proof of infidelity is what brings about Desdemona's death.

clue.text: It holds up glasses showing quality of wine

definitions.meaning: spectacles rest on the bridge of the face's central feature

explanation.surface: Something supporting glasses while a taster assesses a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glasses' suggests wine glasses, but it means spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles rest on the bridge of this facial feature; a wine's aroma is called by the same name.

clue.text: Sea-bird repellent to others

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the bird's name is turned back to front

parts.note: a skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird is off-putting to the rest of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-bird' looks like the definition but supplies the letters; 'others' means other seabirds, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These are also seabirds, so they are other birds besides the skua in the wordplay.

clue.text: Post Office's old character used to herald arrival of mail.

definitions.text: used to herald arrival of mail

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office; with its 's it gives POS
thorn is an Old English letter, a character no longer used

explanation.surface: An old figure at the Post Office once announced that the mail had arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The thorn (þ) was an Old English letter for 'th'; 'character' reads as a person but means a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brass bugle once blown by mail-coach guards to announce the coach's approach.

clue.text: Worthless company girl joined .

parts.note: from the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A firm's female employee is considered of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' suggests a business, but it comes from the proverb that two people make company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costing two old pennies is cheap and of little value, hence trifling.
